name: FigCraft
description: Create and edit interface designs, reusable components and prototypes headlessly; deliver editable FigCraft documents, previews and design exports.
progressive_guidance: The pinned CLI downloads automatically and runs without a desktop window or provider account. For designs based on an existing app, first inspect its components, theme tokens, typography, spacing and representative screens with file/browser tools; use those observed details in the design. Discover command IDs and parameters before constructing edits. Edits stage a native source copy and deliver new conversation artifacts. Commands with explicit paths can still read or write local files: use file, plugin or destructive operations only when requested. Inspect diagnostics, missing fonts and import warnings. Visually inspect the returned preview before delivering the design; use export to check other pages or layers. The native artifact retains components, variables and prototype interactions.

commands.description: Discover installed interface-design commands and accepted parameters, optionally filtered by command ID, label or parameter text.

filter.description: Text to search in the installed command registry.

inspect.description: Read document pages, frame IDs, dimensions, counts, import warnings and missing fonts, or inspect one layer and its immediate children without saving.

inputPath.description: Absolute local source document path. Supports .figcraft and the installed CLI import formats.

nodeId.description: Observed layer or page ID. Omit for a document summary.

fields.description: Exact node property names to inspect, such as fills, fontFamily, layout or interactions. Requires nodeId; cannot combine with outline: true.

outline.description: Return a compact layer tree. Requires nodeId; cannot combine outline: true with fields.

inspect.progressive_guidance: Start with the document summary to discover page and frame IDs. Inspect a page or frame with options.nodeId, then use child IDs for deeper inspection. Request fields when matching styles or checking geometry; outline is useful for names and structure.

edit.description: Create an interface design or edit a source copy with discovered engine commands; deliver an editable .figcraft document and a PNG preview.

params.description: Parameters discovered from the installed command registry.

as.description: Optional name for this step result, referenced by later steps.

inputPath.description: Absolute existing source document. Omit to start a new document.

page.description: Observed page name. Defaults to the first non-divider page.

node.description: Observed layer ID (as a string) or name. Omit to export the whole page.

edit.progressive_guidance: Discover node, frame, layout, component, variable and prototype commands as needed. Steps run as one atomic script; a command failure rolls back document edits. Name a creation step with as, then use {"$ref":"name"} in a later parameter, or {"$step":0} for a prior step index; optional field selects another result field. Build reusable components and auto layout when the design needs them. A new document is already open; file.newFromTemplate can start from an observed template. PNG defaults to the first page; choose preview.page or preview.node to inspect another area. Continue edits from the returned native artifact path. Explicit file commands may have effects outside the staged copy.

export.description: Export a design page or layer as PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG, PDF or Android XML, or the whole document as experimental .fig or Penpot.

inputPath.description: Absolute local source document path. Supports .figcraft and the installed CLI import formats.

format.description: Defaults to png. Raster exports attach bounded visual evidence.

page.description: Observed page name. Defaults to the first non-divider page.

node.description: Observed layer ID (as a string) or name. Omit to export the whole page.

export.progressive_guidance: Without options.node, raster/SVG exports composite the selected page and PDF puts its top-level frames on separate pages. Use observed page names or layer IDs/names. fig and penpot export the whole document and ignore page/layer selectors; inspect diagnostics for unsupported features. Native .figcraft output is available from edit.
